models.collectorNote: Chassis condition and originality of the twin-cam are everything. Big-valve Sprints lead the market; +2s remain the underpriced way in.

generations.name: Elan S1–S4 / Sprint
generations.note: Four-wheel discs, all-independent suspension, and a Ford-block/Cosworth-head twin-cam when rivals had live axles. The Sprint of 1971 is the quick, sorted finale.

models.intro: The definitive Chapman road car: a steel backbone chassis, fibreglass body, twin-cam power, and 675 kg. The Elan's steering feel is still the reference other roadsters are measured against, Mazda benchmarked it for the MX-5.
models.name: Elan

models.collectorNote: V8 cars are appreciating; buy on gearbox and manifold history. The S1 is a design object, purchase the best body, not the cheapest car.

generations.name: Esprit S1
generations.note: Pure origami styling over a 2.0-litre four. Light, delicate, and slow by modern measure, the shape is the point, and The Spy Who Loved Me made it eternal.

generations.name: Esprit V8
generations.note: Lotus's own 3.5 twin-turbo V8, flat-plane crank, 350 hp, and a gearbox that was always the weak link. The Sport 350 is the hardcore farewell.

models.intro: Giugiaro's wedge, Bond's submarine, and 28 years of evolution from a 160 hp four to a twin-turbo V8. The last hand-built Lotus flagship and a study in keeping one design alive.
models.name: Esprit

models.collectorNote: S1s are the collector grade, originality and the early MMC discs matter. Later Toyota-engined cars are the use-it-daily pick. Check the ali tub for accident damage; it is not repairable in the usual way.

generations.name: Elise Series 1
generations.note: Rover's K-series gave 118 hp and the whole car weighed less than a modern car's options list. MMC brake discs and no power steering, brakes, or roof motor.

generations.name: Elise Sprint / Cup
generations.note: Toyota engines replaced the Rover unit, supercharged in the fast cars. The Cup 250 is the track-day distillation; final cars left Hethel in 2021.

models.intro: The car that saved Lotus, named for Romano Artioli's granddaughter. A bonded aluminium tub at 725 kg proved in 1996 that lightness, not power, was the way back.
models.name: Elise

generations.name: Emira V6 / i4
generations.note: The V6 keeps the manual gearbox alive; the AMG i4 is quicker on paper with its dual-clutch. Both sit in a car sized like the Evora it replaced but styled a class above.

models.intro: The last petrol Lotus: AMG's turbo four or Toyota's supercharged V6, hydraulic steering feel, and supercar surfacing at sports-car money. A farewell written with unusual care.
models.name: Emira

generations.name: Evija
generations.note: Developed with Williams Advanced Engineering, targeting the most powerful production car in the world. Deliveries began in 2024 after a long gestation.

models.intro: Lotus's electric reset: four motors, a 2,000 PS target, and Venturi tunnels through the rear bodywork. Eight customer cars a year make it the rarest thing Hethel has built.
models.name: Evija
